Customer to confirm required evidence list and mark mandatory items by 2025-11-14
Schedule technical deep-dive on VPC/private deployment with Priya and Tomás week of 2025-11-17

Tomás Ruiz | Export SOC 2 control mappings and sample audit logs (redacted) | Due: 2025-11-13

summary: Walkthrough of Veridian's vendor security questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ focus). Reviewed SOC 2 artifacts, RBAC/SSO options, KMS/encryption approach, data residency and evidence packaging expectations. Agreed on deliverables and timing for SIG answers and follow-up technical session for private/VPC deployment details.
topics: Encryption at rest/in transit and KMS/HSM integrations
Data residency and on-prem/VPC deployment considerations
meeting_header: Date: 2025-11-07 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 78 minutes | Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE); Priya Desai (Redwood SE); Tomás Ruiz (Redwood SecEng); Dana Kim (Veridian Head of Vendor Risk); Marcus Lee (Veridian InfoSec); Priyanka Shah (Veridian Cloud Arch)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Moran: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick audio check?
[00:06] Dana Kim: Hi, sounds good on my end.
[00:10] Alex Moran: Perfect. I'm Alex, I'm the AE on this account, with Priya our solutions engineer and Tomás from our security team. We put together an agenda — quick walk through your SIG, point to the artifacts we can provide, and then plan next steps.
[00:22] Marcus Lee: Great. We're mainly focused on SIG plus a couple of custom vendor risk items — data residency, and KMS questions.
[00:28] Priyanka Shah: And we want to understand how Redwood would look if we go private VPC versus hosted, specifically audit logs and RBAC.
[00:34] Alex Moran: Totally. We'll start SIG mapping, then SOC 2 / ISO artifacts we can share, then SSO/RBAC and KMS details.
[00:42] [00:42] Tomás Ruiz: Quick note, folks: I'll cover SOC two artifacts — excuse me — SOC 2 artifacts and what sample logs we can provide, and also how we redact customer data in evidence bundles.
[00:51] Dana Kim: Awesome. On the SIG itself, there's a lot flagged as must-have by procurement. We need to mark items that are pass/fail and get evidence for those first.
[01:00] Alex Moran: Understood. In our experience we prioritize the legal/contractual ones, encryption, access control, and auditability. we'll flag those in the sheet.
[01:09] [01:09] Marcus Lee: For encryption, can you confirm where keys live? We require customer-managed keys for certain workloads.
[01:15] Tomás Ruiz: Yes. For our Private and Dedicated offerings we support BYOK via KMS integrations — AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and we have an HSM path for on-prem integrations. For hosted Tier we also offer envelope encryption and can provide a customer-managed KMS option on enterprise contracts; there's an extra integration step.
[01:34] Priya Desai: To add, the console shows key usage per-route in the audit logs. We can export logs that show key IDs referenced by operation, we'll include an example.
[01:42] Dana Kim: That would help. We need both proof and a runbook for rotation and key compromise procedures.
[01:49] Tomás Ruiz: We have rotation docs and templated playbooks; I'll attach a redacted sample. The rotation follows industry best practices and we can show the rotation event in logs.
[01:58] [01:58] Alex Moran: Switching to SOC 2 — Tomás, do you want to walk high level and then we'll map to the SIG?
[02:03] Tomás Ruiz: Sure. Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering Security and Availability at present; we're working toward CC and maybe ISO-27001 next year. The SOC 2 report is done annually and includes control narratives, test matrices, and a sample of system-generated logs. We can share the report under NDA and we can also provide attestations and a vendor pack with redacted logs.
[02:26] Marcus Lee: When you say redacted logs, what's the level of redaction? We can't have customer PII in third-party bundles.
[02:32] Tomás Ruiz: Good question. We remove token strings and direct user identifiers, replace with stable pseudonyms, and truncate payloads. The ICC — I mean, in practice the logs retain timestamps, operation names, and resource IDs, which are enough for verification.
[02:46] [02:46] Priya Desai: Also note some of the logs come from the serving runtime — those include latency, model-version, and route metadata. If you need content-level logs we do have an option but it's tightly controlled and typically requires a legal/data processing addendum.
[02:59] Dana Kim: We'll flag content-level logging as a red line — only permitted under contractual terms with strong access controls.
[03:05] [03:05] Alex Moran: Let's talk RBAC and SSO. What kinds of SAML and SCIM flows do you support?
[03:10] Priya Desai: We support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Roles are mapped to internal RBAC policies; you can have org-level admins, project-level engineers, read-only auditors, and token-scoped service accounts. We also support session expiry policies and MFA enforced via IdP.
[03:27] Marcus Lee: How are API keys handled? Can we restrict keys to read-only embeddings or generation-only scopes?
[03:33] Priya Desai: Yes, token scopes are granular. You can create keys limited to embeddings-only, read-only, or generation with per-route limits and TTL. Keys are stored encrypted at rest and only decrypted in memory for request handling.
[03:45] [03:45] Dana Kim: For evidence, can you provide role-mapping screenshots and a CSV export of audit events tied to role changes?
[03:52] Tomás Ruiz: Yes, we can provide an audit export — we'll redact personal emails. We'll provide the RBAC mapping spreadsheet and a sample CSV of role assignment events.
[04:01] [04:01] Priyanka Shah: On the private deployment side, network segmentation is key for us. If we run Redwood in our VPC, where do audit logs live?
[04:09] Priya Desai: In VPC/private deployments audit logs can be routed to your logging endpoint (e.g., CloudWatch, Stackdriver, or an on-prem SIEM). That means they never leave your environment unless you choose to stream them elsewhere.
[04:20] Marcus Lee: And is the private control plane fully isolated? We need to know the control plane path for updates and telemetry.
[04:26] Tomás Ruiz: There are two patterns: fully air-gapped on-prem, or private control plane that communicates over a customer-managed egress with mutual TLS. For the latter, we provide an ops agent with a small set of outbound endpoints and ports; we can provide the allowlist for your firewall.
[04:40] [04:40] Dana Kim: Please put that allowlist in the evidence pack.
[04:43] Alex Moran: Will do. Switching back to the SIG: the sheet you sent had about 120 line items. Our plan is to triage into three buckets — contractual (must-have), technical (need evidence), and informational (notes). We'll pre-fill the first pass.
[04:58] Priya Desai: We'll also add a column for the artifact type: report, screenshot, runbook, config snippet, or log sample.
[05:06] [05:06] Marcus Lee: For the config snippets, sometimes we need proof that KV cache or other runtime components don't leak secrets. Do you have architecture diagrams?
[05:14] Priya Desai: Yes, we have architecture diagrams that show KV cache boundaries and memory encryption behavior. Note that some diagrams are sensitive; we'll replace hostnames with placeholders in shared copies.
[05:24] Tomás Ruiz: Also worth noting: runtime memory isn't persisted to disk for KV cache — it's in GPU memory; we can provide concrete statements and some test artifacts showing wipe on restart.
[05:35] [05:35] Dana Kim: That addresses a lot. For data residency: Veridian operates in EU and APAC; we need assurances that data doesn't cross regions. How granular is routing?
[05:44] Alex Moran: We support region pinning per-tenant and per-route. For Dedicated and Private we can deploy in-region capacity. Hosted customers can specify preferred region and we provide SLA-backed region routing for enterprise tiers.
[05:58] Priyanka Shah: If you need strict residency for training or retention, we also have configurable retention policies at the tenancy level.
[06:06] [06:06] Marcus Lee: On retention, do you allow zero-retention for certain workloads?
[06:10] Tomás Ruiz: We have privacy modes where content-level logs are not stored and only ephemeral KV is used. Those modes are supported in private/dedicated environments; for hosted we have a data-retention setting and a documented deletion process.
[06:23] Dana Kim: Good. Now about CAIQ: do you have a pre-populated CAIQ we can ingest?
[06:28] Alex Moran: Yes — we keep canonical CAIQ and SIG mappings. We'll export a CAIQ/consensus sheet with our responses and include cross-references to SOC 2 controls and evidence items.
[06:38] [06:38] Priya Desai: Example: CAIQ item about key management will reference SOC 2 control A.2.x and the KMS runbook artifact.
[06:46] Marcus Lee: For the legal team, we might need encryption certs or attestations. Can you provide public cert chains for your HSMs?
[06:53] Tomás Ruiz: We can provide certificate chains and attestations for our managed HSM provider; for BYOK we'd help you configure either our HSM or integrate with your on-cloud KMS.
[07:02] [07:02] Priya Shah: Regarding evidence packaging, what's the expected format? Do you prefer one big zip or a drive with folders and a manifest?
[07:08] Alex Moran: We usually provide a Drive folder with subfolders per control family and a manifest spreadsheet linking items to SIG/CAIQ rows. That keeps it scalable and searchable.
[07:18] Dana Kim: Drive is fine. Send a manifest so our procurement can crosswalk quickly.
[07:23] [07:23] Marcus Lee: A quick question on incident history: procurement wants to see incident reports and timelines for major incidents in the last 24 months. Are those shareable?
[07:31] Tomás Ruiz: Yes, we have a redacted incident report pack that summarizes impact, root cause, and mitigations. We'll share redacted versions and timeline artefacts.
[07:41] [07:41] Alex Moran: There's also often a licensing/compliance question around logging retention for auditors. We can include the retention policy for each deployment mode.
[07:48] Priyanka Shah: And for SIEM integration, we can produce an example event mapping to your fields.
[07:54] [07:54] Dana Kim: That'd be helpful. Procurement also wants to understand support SLAs for evidence requests in a legal review window.
[08:01] Alex Moran: For enterprise contracts we define support windows and priority for evidence requests; normally we commit to a 7–10 business day turn for standard evidence and faster for critical items. We'll note that in the pack and include contract language examples.
[08:14] [08:14] Marcus Lee: On the point of live demos vs evidence, sometimes our team requests a live demo to validate controls. Are you open to a controlled demo environment?
[08:22] Priya Desai: Yes. We can spin up a demo tenant with pre-configured logs and controls, share temporary credentials, and do a guided walkthrough. That avoids sharing production logs.
[08:33] Tomás Ruiz: We'll make sure the demo tenant is instrumented to show RBAC changes, key rotation, and audit trails.
[08:40] [08:40] Dana Kim: Good. One of our procurement questions is about subcontractors — do you use third-party service providers for telemetry or observability?
[08:47] Alex Moran: We use a small set of observability vendors and cloud providers; we'll include a subcontractor list with the purpose and whether they have access to content. Most telemetry vendors process metadata only.
[08:58] [08:58] Marcus Lee: Any concerns about vendor risk from those subs?
[09:01] Tomás Ruiz: We do vendor risk assessments and require subcontractors to meet our baseline security requirements; for high-risk subs we have DPA clauses and additional audit rights.
[09:10] [09:10] Priya Shah: Another practical item — does Redwood provide a change history for the runtime and model versions? Our auditors ask for model-change logs.
[09:18] Priya Desai: Yes, we maintain model versioning and release notes; we can provide a model-change ledger showing rollout dates, canary windows, and rollback events.
[09:27] Dana Kim: Put that in the manifest.
[09:30] [09:30] Alex Moran: We're about halfway through our slot, maybe we do a quick recap and then mark action items?
[09:35] Marcus Lee: Sounds good.
[09:36] [09:36] Alex Moran: Recap: Redwood will pre-fill SIG/CAIQ with answers, provide SOC 2 report under NDA, redacted logs, RBAC exports, KMS runbook, allowlist for VPC agent, and incident report pack. Veridian will finalize which CAIQ rows are must-have and share vendor evidence template. We'll schedule a technical deep-dive the week of 2025-11-17.
[09:58] Dana Kim: That aligns with our expectations.
[10:01] [10:01] Priya Desai: One last note: on the hosted side, for customers with stricter requirements we recommend Dedicated + BYOK as the fastest path to satisfy KMS and residency controls. Private on-prem is available if you need full isolation.
[10:16] Marcus Lee: Good to know.
[10:18] [10:18] Dana Kim: Thanks — Alex, Priya, Tomás. We'll wait for the sheet and artifacts.
[10:23] Alex Moran: We'll aim to get the first bundle to you by 2025-11-12. Thanks everyone.
[10:27] [10:27] Meeting end.
